key_insight: The reported gains in non-invasive brain-to-text decoding are largely explained by a timing shortcut from overlapping word windows, and removing it reveals the true benefit of brain-derived signals.
engineering_relevance: For robust decoding systems, independently encoding each word window and combining repeated observations with a pretrained language model can substantially improve performance without leaking timing information.
method: Encode each brain window independently instead of jointly across a sentence.
Aggregate predictions from multiple neural responses to the same word.
Use a pretrained LLM as a linguistic prior during decoding.
evidence_signal: The shortcut-sensitive method scored 22.0% balanced accuracy on synthetic no-brain signals versus 22.3% on real brain recordings, while the revised SimpleB2T reached 36.6% word error rate with five observations per word on the perceived-speech benchmark.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful windowing and evaluation design, because overlapping segments can silently leak word-duration information and inflate apparent decoding quality.
paper_title: Removing Timing Shortcuts Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
